rows.notes: Plant reached commercial production in Aug 2022 (Green Review, 13 Aug 2022) so status stays 'operational' (furthest stage reached) but project_state = cancelled: WSKG 2024-10-21 reports most employees laid off and the state agency says operations paused; Chapter 11 filed 2025-01-27 (Delaware 25-10131), dismissed 2025-06-26 after a court-authorized asset sale and wind-down (ElevenFlo, a SECONDARY case tracker; the Stretto claims site confirms the dismissal order but gives no sale detail); equipment auctioned June 2025 (HGP). The v1 note that Musashi Auto Parts bought the assets for ~$10M is from the same secondary tracker/search summaries and was not seen on a primary page - not stored. Nameplate 1.8 GWh = plant capacity in 2022 reporting; ref_year 2022 = publication-year fallback, searched (no dated full-capacity statement). The 'expand to 38 GWh by 2030' aspiration is undated-structure and excluded (D-015). v1 chemistry 'LFP' not confirmed: source says lithium mixed-metal phosphate (LMP) with biomineralisation -> 'other'. v1 capacity_by_year {2022:1, 2023:1.8}, jv_partners, end_market, cell_format could not be confirmed on pages I could open -> null. installed capacity: no sourced figure and plant closed -> null.

Lyten HQ/'Baytech' pilot site: Lyten says it is the 'first semi-automated lithium-sulfur battery manufacturing pilot line in the US' (company operations page, undated) and (Feb 2025 release) that it is producing NDAA-compliant Li-S cells in San Jose. Pilot scale only. v1 nameplate 0.2 GWh removed: the '200 MWh' target was attributed to San Jose + San Leandro combined in Nov 2024/Feb 2025 coverage and the company's own page now gives >150 MWh for San Leandro alone, so no San Jose-only GWh figure is sourced. start_year 2023 (v1) not confirmable verbatim -> null. Chemistry is lithium-sulfur -> 'other'. cell_format / end_market unconfirmed -> null. No dated news after Feb 2025 on this specific pilot line, hence 0.5.

FY2025 10-K: facility being renovated 'to support up to 2 GWh of cell, module, and pack capacity'; construction suspended Q2 2024 for lack of funding; pivot from NMC to LFP; only a pack assembly line added late 2025 (deliveries from the pack line expected 2026). Q1 2026 call (2026-05-11): resumption of full-scale construction 'remains contingent upon securing additional financing and strategic partnerships' -> paused. No cell production (all active cell capacity is Huzhou, China). Nameplate 2 GWh is cell+module+pack design figure; v1 mention of ~8 GWh future expansion not sourced here and excluded (aspiration). ref_year 2026 = publication-year fallback, searched (no target year; project paused). v1 announced_year 2021, cell_format pouch, end_market mixed not confirmed on fetched pages -> null. 10-K published date = EDGAR directory last-modified 2026-03-16.

Chico 2 (50,000 sq ft, Chico CA): Dec 2023 press release says the 18650 cells are 'manufactured exclusively' at Chico 2 and the plant 'will go into full production in early 2024'; 21700 planned from 2025 at 30,000 cells/day. No news found after Jan 2024 (searched 2026) -> status/operation unconfirmed since, confidence capped low. Nameplate: company says '150MW' - a power rating, not GWh/yr; v1's conversion to 0.15 GWh was an interpretation -> nameplate set null (Ah/MW are not GWh/yr). start_year 2024 = stated full-production target, weak. Chemistry graphene-enhanced Li-ion -> 'other'. end_market unconfirmed -> null.

Plant started commercial-scale operations in 2024 (company release Apr 2024; CHARGED repost dated 2024-06-24) then Natron ceased operations: closure of Holland (and Santa Clara) effective 2025-09-03 (Manufacturing Dive, 2025-09-08: 'permanently close its facilities in Holland, Michigan'; also halts the planned Rocky Mount NC gigafactory), and Holland equipment was auctioned by Tiger Group (bidding closes 2025-11-13). Status = operational (reached), project_state = cancelled. Company capacity '600 MW/yr' is a power figure -> nameplate null. end_market / cell_format not confirmed on fetched pages -> null. Candidate-routing duplicate of this row (existing_id) - no new row added.

Pilot-line LFP cell production began Nov 2023 (Solar Power World, 2023-11-01) - status operational at pilot scale. Jan 7 2026: ONE 'exits automotive EV, suspending its multiyear investment in the passenger EV market', pivots to rail/defence/grid storage; says the Van Buren cell line 'has completed retooling' for a new LFP cell (company release). Sept 2026 (Michigan Public): state incentive cut from $200M to $150M, jobs cut to 1,606 across Van Buren + Novi, timeline pushed 2030 -> 2037. => project_state paused for the original 20 GWh build-out. NAMEPLATE: v1 20 GWh (2022 announcement; 2023 article said the 20-GWh line would launch 'next year') is superseded by the 2026 pivot/revised state agreement, none of which states a GWh figure; per D-017 I treat it as an aspiration and set nameplate null (old figure: 20 GWh, ref year 2027). ESCALATE: lead may prefer to keep 20 GWh with project_state paused (D-014). Installed: v1 timeline says 10 MWh pilot but no page I could open states a MWh figure -> null. Some search snippets (not opened) say ONE is vacating most of the Van Buren building - not used. v1 capacity_timeline is unverified and should be dropped by the lead. Michigan Public article says only grid storage, rail and defense contracts, hence end_market mixed.

Peak's own release: the 183,000 sq ft Sacramento facility 'will produce up to 4 GWh of battery systems annually' and Peak will 'pair GM's next-generation sodium-ion cell technology with Peak's proprietary energy storage platform' - system integration, cells come from GM (GM labs in Michigan per press). Announced 2026-07-08 (v1 said 9 July). 4 GWh is system output, not cell output.

Eagle Line (QSE-5 solid-state cells, Cobra separator process) inaugurated 2026-02-04 at the San Jose HQ for 'highly automated pilot production of battery cells' for OEM sampling (Electrek). Pilot only; QS licenses to partners (VW/PowerCo) for GWh-scale, so no GWh capacity -> null. The BusinessWire release (v1 source) returned 403; Electrek is the opened source. No post-Feb-2026 ramp update found. end_market (v1 EV) / cell_format not confirmed -> null.

Aug 2022: 79,000 sq ft San Jose engineering/printing hub; Sakuu 'recently opened a pilot production line, which is currently producing batteries for clients' (CHARGED, 2022-08-16). Sakuu's Oct 2025 release (opened) says a validation cell 'is manufactured on Sakuu Kavian' but does not say where. Pilot scale; v1 nameplate 1.0 GWh and {2021:0.0025, 2022:1} ramp are NOT supported (60 GWh by 2028 refers to future gigafactories) -> nameplate and by-year null. Chemistry 'solid-state' (3D-printed solid-state battery per CHARGED). end_market EV (v1) unconfirmed -> null. No 2026 news on the pilot line -> low confidence.

Woburn MA is SES AI's R&D site (Q3 2026 release dateline WOBURN; company says it is 'headquartered in Boston and with NDAA-compliant manufacturing plant in Chungju, South Korea' - commercial manufacturing is in Korea, not here). An Oct 2026 job listing for Woburn says the role will 'lead and manage all aspects of pilot-scale cell manufacturing and prototype execution', so prototype/pilot cell building exists at Woburn - kept as a low-confidence pilot row, status weakly supported. No capacity figure; chemistry (v1 lithium-metal), format, end_market not confirmed on pages I could open -> null. ALTERNATIVE (not chosen): remove as not_cell (R&D/HQ only; v1 is_cell_manufacturer=False) - I had no positive evidence that Woburn makes no cells. Chungju (SES's real cell line, 1M NDAA drone cells/yr installed) has no row in factories_export.csv under an SES id; see Discoveries.

EV cell pilot line installed and announced May/June 2022, 'expected to be capable of producing 300 cells per week' (EV Report repost of the company release; ~15,000 cells/yr is my arithmetic and not stated) - pilot line, no GWh figure. Still active in Q3 2026: company cites 'cell-testing and pilot-production capabilities' (2026-11-03), SK On Line Installation Agreement completed (Q2 2026 release via Yahoo, page not re-opened for a quote). Separate continuous-electrolyte (MOBIUS) line is a materials line and is not this row. cell_format pouch and end_market EV carried from v1 (v1 notes cite the Solid Power release, which I could not open - 403); lower weight. Thornton CO electrolyte plant is materials, out of scope.

54 GWh / ~$4bn plan announced Apr 2022; 135 acres bought near the Salton Sea Jan 2023 (pv magazine USA). Searches (English, plus Imperial County/CEQA/permit angles) found NO news after early 2023: no groundbreaking, permit or financing report; founder previously guided groundbreaking Aug/Sep 2024 and first batteries ~18 months later - both dates passed with nothing found. Kept 'announced', project_state active (no source says paused/cancelled) but silence suggests stalled. ref_year 2023 = publication-year fallback, searched (source gives no production year; v1's 2026 was loader-inferred). v1 mixed end_market, 'lithium-ion' chemistry not confirmed -> null. ESCALATE: 54 GWh row at 0.35 (gate G4) - no further evidence exists in open sources.

12,000 sq ft Sorrento Valley pilot/LRIP sodium-ion cell line funded by a CEC RAMP grant (~$2.99M, project kick-off Apr 2025 per search results). San Diego EDC case study (June 2025): company 'completed construction work on its San Diego manufacturing facility' and plans to commission it in Q1 2026 (MWh-scale output). No page I opened confirms commissioning happened; Jan 2026 pv magazine says Unigrid 'relies on Asian production facilities for the bulk of its manufacturing' (100 MWh/yr via foundries, 1 GWh target 2026 - NOT San Diego capacity). Kept under_construction (commissioning unconfirmed). No GWh/yr figure for the San Diego line -> null. cell_format, end_market not confirmed -> null.

Status unconfirmed.
